questions.q: A `@Transactional` service method throws a checked `IOException` and nothing else is configured. What happens to the transaction?
o: It commits, as only unchecked exceptions and errors roll back
It rolls back, because any exception rolls back
It rolls back only if the exception is in `throws`
It stays open until the caller decides
questions.w: By default Spring rolls back on RuntimeException and Error only. Use `rollbackFor = Exception.class` to include checked exceptions.

questions.q: `transfer()` is `@Transactional` and calls `this.audit()` in the same class. `audit()` is `@Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW)`. What happens?
o: `audit()` joins the same transaction, as the call skips the proxy
`audit()` starts a new, independent transaction as annotated
Spring throws an exception about the annotation at startup
`audit()` runs with no transaction at all, not even a joined one
questions.w: The transaction advice lives in a proxy. A call on `this` is a plain method call, so the annotation on the inner method is ignored. Move it to another bean.

questions.q: An outer `REQUIRED` method catches a `RuntimeException` thrown by an inner `REQUIRED` method and returns normally. What does the commit do?
o: It fails with `UnexpectedRollbackException`: the transaction is rollback-only
It succeeds and saves all of the work done by the outer method
It succeeds but silently skips only the work of the inner method
It retries the inner method once and then commits the result
questions.w: REQUIRED joins one physical transaction. The inner failure marks it rollback-only, and catching the exception does not clear that mark.

questions.q: Which propagation suits an audit record that must be saved even if the main business transaction rolls back?
o: `REQUIRES_NEW`
`REQUIRED`
`MANDATORY`
`SUPPORTS`
questions.w: REQUIRES_NEW suspends the outer transaction and commits independently on its own connection.

questions.q: You publish a message to a broker inside a `@Transactional` method just before it returns. What is the main risk?
o: The consumer may act before commit, or the transaction may roll back
The broker rejects any message that is sent inside a transaction
The message is always delivered twice by the broker
The transaction cannot commit while a message is being sent
questions.w: Use `@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` for simple cases or the transactional outbox for guaranteed delivery.

questions.q: Why is calling a slow remote service inside a transaction a problem?
o: It holds a pooled connection and locks, so slow calls exhaust the pool
Remote calls are simply not allowed inside any transaction
The remote call is rolled back automatically by Spring
It turns the whole transaction into a read-only one
questions.w: Keep transactions short: no remote calls, file I/O or waiting inside them.

questions.q: A method annotated `@Async` and `@Transactional` is called from another bean. In which transaction does the async body run?
o: In its own new transaction on the async thread
In the caller's transaction
In no transaction at all
In one transaction shared by all async threads
questions.w: The transaction is bound to a thread. The caller's transaction does not follow the work onto another thread.

o: Nothing strict: a hint that skips dirty checking, may use a replica
Any attempt to write always throws an exception right away
The method runs without any transaction being started
The transaction is run with SERIALIZABLE isolation instead
questions.w: readOnly is an optimisation hint, not a security or integrity mechanism.
